setup: A function built from sin([[a]]x) or cos([[a]]x), or from x sin([[a]]x), is differentiated several times, and its value at x = 0 is asked for.

steps.say: The chain rule brings down a factor of [[a]] at every differentiation, because the inner function is [[a]]x.
Each derivative moves along the cycle sine, cosine, minus sine, minus cosine, and four steps bring the cycle back to its start.
At x = 0 the sine is 0 and the cosine is 1, so the surviving term is a power of [[a]] times 1, 0 or -1, or twice [[a]] when the function also carries a factor of x.
